passages.provision_quote: Resentencing pursuant to this section shall result in a lesser sentence than the one originally imposed as a result of the elimination of the repealed enhancement, unless the court finds by clear and convincing evidence that imposing a lesser sentence would endanger public safety.
passages.note: Authored bill invalidating prior sentence enhancements and ordering resentencing to a lesser sentence; it lowers punishment but names no support, treatment, service or restitution.

rows.reasoning: Allen authored SB 483 (2021-2022), which declares prior prison-term and controlled-substance sentence enhancements legally invalid and requires courts to recall and resentence so the result is a lesser sentence. That shows a lean away from harsher punishment, but it establishes neither "Focus on support and treatment, not punishment." nor "Give the person a chance to make things right through service or restitution, rarely punishment." — the bill provides no support, treatment, service or restitution, and it does not separate those rungs from "Each situation is different — some people need support, some need consequences."
needs_source: Benjamin Allen's own words in his current term on how the system should respond when someone breaks the law (floor statement, questionnaire or issue page), and any authored or sponsored California Senate bill that funds treatment, diversion or restitution rather than incarceration
